title: The Healthy Paranoia of Anticipating Change
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that leaders must constantly balance the risk of moving too fast against the risk of moving too slowly as markets and technology shift. Moving too quickly creates anxiety, waste, and instability; moving too slowly costs market share and leaves organizations vulnerable to competitors who fill emerging gaps. The author frames the goal as 'adaptive speed' rather than perfect timing, and highlights strategic inflection points -- often signaled by shifting financial data or customers asking for things outside the current model -- as the moments that separate leaders who adapt from those who deny. It closes by invoking Andy Grove's dictum that only the paranoid survive.
points: Moving too fast risks instability and vulnerability to competitors; moving too slow risks lost market share and customer churn.
The goal isn't perfect timing but 'adaptive speed' -- fast enough to stay relevant, deliberate enough to stay smart.
Strategic inflection points are most often signaled by a marked shift in financial or productivity data.
Customers or users asking for things outside the current model is an early warning sign that a new competitor may soon meet that unmet demand.
quotes: Moving too quickly on change can create team member anxiety, customer confusion, resource waste, and operational breakdowns.
